chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub, from Bukayr ibn A'yn, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

'Shall I not narrate to you the ablution of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' So he took a handful of water with his right palm and washed his face with it. Then he took with his left hand a handful of water and washed his right hand with it. Then he took with his right hand a handful of water and washed his left hand with it. Then he wiped with the remainder of his two hands his head and his feet.
ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step procedure for performing wudu according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi provides a concise, practical model of the Prophet’s ablution, emphasizing the economy of water by using the same water for washing the hands and wiping the head and feet. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration is often cited to support the permissibility of wiping over the feet (masah) rather than washing them, highlighting the distinction between the Prophet’s practice and the later codified legal rulings. It underscores the spiritual discipline of moderation (iqtisad) in ritual purity.
